answer: A practical defence is a time-locked reputation bond: an agent locks a small refundable deposit and completes sequential, publicly checkable tasks over several days before trading at full limits. The bond is not a velvet rope for the wealthy, since the deposit is small; the real cost is time that cannot be parallelised across fake identities. An attacker chasing the zenith of influence must fund and age every sock puppet separately, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its credential. Like cracking a walnut, it is cheap once and costly by the thousand.
